summary: 1964 state-built 809R fire tower in Tulare County; sources disagree on its closure (late 1970s or late 1980s), a 2018 assessment found it in surprisingly good condition apart from roof, siding and window damage, and it stands behind locked gates.

facts.design: 809R building design with a 30 foot steel tower of three floors and a working cab
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Tulare Unit (Cal Fire TUU)

access.note: Not accessible to the general public; about 5 miles from paved road, behind locked gates (Register description, carries an MVT 10/91 note)

events.note: Built by the state of California in 1964
Buck Rock Foundation assessment visit: overall good condition apart from damage to roofing and siding and several broken windows; interior fire equipment removed
Registered October 30, 2019 as US 1370, CA 193; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.current: 2017 restored (CAL FIRE began a refurbishment of the lookout)
corrections.proposed: Remove; no source read supports a 2017 refurbishment
corrections.why: The 2018 Buck Rock text quoted on the Register says CAL FIRE's priority was to preserve the structure while it considered future use. No page read describes 2017 work. The PDF the record cites (cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf) returned almost no text, so its claim could not be checked.

corrections.current: 2018 restored (Buck Rock Foundation volunteers repaired the roof)
corrections.proposed: 2018 assessed: roofing and siding damaged, several windows broken
corrections.why: The Buck Rock 2018 assessment quoted on the Register describes roof damage. No page read says the roof was repaired.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Buck Rock text on the Register says the tower was shuttered in the late 1980s. Peakbagging's 2008 photo note says it was last occupied in the late 1970s. Both are shown as sources' claims; no year is given in events.

The Register says the lookout is on private land in the Eshom Valley area. Peakbagging says the summit area is California state property and most surrounding land is private. The record does not settle ownership.
The Register gives 4,381 ft (1,335 m); Peakbagging gives 3480 ft. The record keeps the Register figure, which it also matches.

notes_for_editor: The brief's Boucher Hill duplicate claim and 2017 refurbishment both come from cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf, which returned only 5 characters of text, so they are unverified and left out of events; the Boucher Hill claim does not appear in any page read. The locked-gates and radio-repeater sentences on the Register carry an MVT 10/91 note, so they may describe a 1991 visit. The Forest Lookouts Shadequarter page held only navigation text. Public access is marked restricted from the Register's description, not from a current visit. The FFLA list shows the tower as standing; no 2025 visit report was found.
